access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: This package is a library with no user interface. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml runs the test suite on every push to main and every pull request that changes anything but prose, and its aggregate job is a required check. A pull request that changes only prose files nothing built reads skips the suite, and the aggregate check still passes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses common tools: uv, hatchling, cffi and CMake, with the platform's C compiler. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md#build
build_floss_tools_justification: The project builds with FLOSS tools alone: uv, hatchling, cffi, CMake and GCC or Clang. Only the static Windows wheels use MSVC. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md#build
build_non_recursive_justification: The vendored build is a single cmake invocation over one CMakeLists.txt tree (scripts/cffi_build.py), not a recursive make over independent subdirectory builds. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/scripts/cffi_build.py
build_preserve_debug_justification: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE set to RelWithDebInfo or Debug builds the vendored library with debug information, and CFLAGS reaches the extension's compile. Release is the default, which every published wheel builds. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/scripts/README.md#environment-variables
build_repeatable_justification: wheel-reproducibility.yml builds each platform's wheel twice, for one interpreter, and requires the two archives to match byte for byte, after cibuildwheel's repair step as well. It also builds on a second image per platform, with a different toolchain, and compares the two. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/wheel-reproducibility.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit, and sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds a release from its signed tag and verifies the rebuilt file against the release's own PyPI attestation; RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. Compiled wheels are rebuilt and compared byte for byte by wheel-reproducibility.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: Outside Windows, the static extension's compile and link honour CC, CFLAGS, CPPFLAGS, LDSHARED and LDFLAGS as setuptools composes them, as scripts/README.md documents. CMake reads CC and CFLAGS for the vendored library. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/scripts/README.md#environment-variables
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, almost all of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review and has since made four small changes. No person outside the owners has committed to this repository. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run in .pre-commit-config.yaml, which the required lint check runs on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. pmazzocchi has made four small changes. pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. No person outside the owners has committed to this repository. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: These are bindings to libsecp256k1, which implements one curve, and Bitcoin's consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes. Another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: calls libsecp256k1, does not reimplement it
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: This tree performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
crypto_credential_agility_justification: These are bindings with no configuration file or credential store: a secret scalar or nonce is a caller-supplied value or buffer, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
crypto_keylength_justification: libsecp256k1 has one curve, secp256k1, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
crypto_published_justification: FFI bindings to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1 (and secp256k1-zkp), which implement published algorithms: ECDSA, BIP340 Schnorr, ECDH
crypto_random_justification: ECDSA nonces are libsecp256k1's RFC 6979; BIP340 aux_rand32, context randomization, the MuSig session secrand and ElligatorSwift entropy default to secrets.token_bytes(32) when the caller supplies none. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/_scalar.py
crypto_tls12_justification: btclib-secp256k1 uses no TLS: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tree/main/src/btclib_secp256k1
crypto_used_network_justification: btclib-secp256k1 does not use the network: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tree/main/src/btclib_secp256k1
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: This tree performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The bindings expose libsecp256k1's ECDSA with RFC 6979 nonces, BIP340 Schnorr signatures and BIP327 MuSig2, each SHA-256-based by its specification; there is no caller-configurable cipher and no SHA-1. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/dsa.py
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution channels (GitHub, PyPI) use HTTPS exclusively.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/ https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot security updates are on, and Dependabot's weekly version updates cover uv, github-actions, the ClusterFuzzLite image and the vendored libsecp256k1 and secp256k1-zkp submodules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: btclib-secp256k1 is a set of Python bindings to libsecp256k1, Bitcoin Core's C library for secp256k1. It signs and verifies with ECDSA and BIP340 Schnorr. https://btclib.org/btclib-secp256k1/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, linked to this project's page. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the module layout and layer boundaries of this tree's software. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_current_justification: docs.yml builds the docs with -W -n on every pull request, and the build is a required check. The API reference is generated from the shipped docstrings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md gives the install command and a Quickstart that tests/examples_test.py runs, so a stale example fails the suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations of the binding layer* section states which secret buffers libsecp256k1 zeroizes and which stay in Python objects that cannot be zeroized, the caller-owned `into=` buffers that close part of that gap, and what a scalar's magnitude can leak. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The test suite runs under pytest with assertions enabled (Python's -O is never used), so every assert in the code and tests is checked on every run. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree vendors and compiles libsecp256k1, C code, and fuzz.yml runs ClusterFuzzLite over the bindings' entry points with sanitizer: address (AddressSanitizer), weekly and on dispatch. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
external_dependencies_justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: The organization's GOVERNANCE.md documents how decisions are made and every role. This tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: https://btclib.org/btclib-secp256k1/ is served over HTTPS with Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security. The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/ sends all but the CSP; that is PyPI's to set. The documentation site https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options; that is Read the Docs' to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-01.
hardening_justification: The compiled wheels are built with hardening flags and read back for them. scripts/cffi_build.py builds a stack protector and FORTIFY_SOURCE on Linux and macOS; on Linux, immediate binding (-z now), a read-only relocation segment and, on x86_64 glibc, the CET marking; /GS and control flow guard on MSVC; ASLR, DEP and high entropy for the mingw-w64 DLL. test.yml runs .github/scripts/verify_wheel_contents.py over every built wheel and refuses one that lacks a property. The first release built so is v0.8.0.13. The CET and BTI marking is not asked of aarch64 and musllinux wheels, whose C runtime does not carry it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/docs/source/package-content-policy.md#what-the-compiled-file-has-to-be-built-with https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues/1194
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section argues how each principle applies to the binding layer, and SECURITY.md's *Limitations of the binding layer* states where that layer stops. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles
input_validation_justification: Each wrapper checks sizes and ranges at the cffi boundary before a pointer reaches C and refuses anything of the wrong length or form; whether the bytes are a valid key, point or signature is left to libsecp256k1, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_common_justification: btclib-secp256k1 is on PyPI, so pip install and pip uninstall install and remove it. README.md gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: After git submodule update --init, uv sync --locked installs the whole development environment and builds the extension. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives both. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is pip install, which follows pip's own install-location conventions; the project has no installer of its own. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: This package is a library and produces no text for end users; its output is bytes and integers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md
know_common_errors_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md argues how each common implementation weakness of a binding layer (CWE-125, 787, 20, 208, 362 and others) is countered in this tree. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#common-implementation-weaknesses
know_secure_design_justification: fametrano, the primary developer, maintains ASSURANCE_CASE.md, whose Secure design principles section applies each principle to this code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles
license_per_file_justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/__init__.py
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: The only workflow_dispatch input is verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name reaches steps only through env:, and is checked against the package version before the release is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique version: libsecp256k1's M.N.P, plus a fourth number for a release of the bindings alone, set by a v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that differs from the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release file carries the version in its name: the sdist and the wheels on PyPI, and the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle on the GitHub release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/
osps_br_04_01_justification: Every release has a CHANGELOG.md entry, listing every change, and a RELEASE_NOTES.md entry, listing what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. The GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. Every build that ships takes its build requirements from build-constraints.txt, exported from uv.lock with hashes. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. Every GitHub release from v0.8.0 on carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle for its sdist. Release tags are signed from v0.8.0 on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: The user documentation is README.md's Quickstart, which tests/examples_test.py runs, plus the API reference rendered from the docstrings at https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io.
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verify command pins the signer: --owner and a comparison of the certificate's repository id name this repository, --signer-workflow the workflow that signed, which SECURITY.md names for each release, and --source-ref the release tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: pyproject.toml gives the reason for each runtime dependency. uv obtains them from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. The vendored C libraries are git submodules pinned by commit, which Dependabot also tracks. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv and a C toolchain are the prerequisites, git submodule update --init fetches the vendored libraries, and uv sync --locked builds the environment and the extension. README.md's *Build* says what each platform needs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage questions are discussed publicly in the repository's issues, which have a question form, and pull requests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, tests against external vectors, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: LICENSE ships at the sdist root and in every wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. From v0.8.0.10 on, each wheel also carries libsecp256k1's COPYING, and the sdist carries the COPYING of both vendored libraries. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/#files
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature. main refuses force-pushes and requires linear history. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies, the runtime one and the development groups, and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every release from v0.8.0.7 on attaches a CycloneDX SBOM of the sdist, covered by the release attestation. Every wheel from v0.8.0.10 on carries its own, at .dist-info/sboms/btclib_secp256k1.cdx.json. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main requires the six CI status checks. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's *Which repositories, and how far* lists every btclib-org repository and its tier. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: libsecp256k1 comes from bitcoin-core/secp256k1, which this project does not administer. The sdist also ships secp256k1-zkp from the fork fametrano/secp256k1-zkp, and no wheel carries it. The fork's branches are unprotected, so what ships is the one commit the submodule pins by sha, and the pin moves only through a pull request here, under main's rules. Every publish job needs zkp-pin. It checks that the pinned commit is the one README.md names and documents, that it is at most one commit ahead of BlockstreamResearch/secp256k1-zkp's master, and that every commit ahead carries a valid signature from fametrano's or Andrew Poelstra's key. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/zkp-pin.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.gitmodules
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary files are fuzz seed inputs and the Sphinx inventory python.inv. The vendored C libraries are git submodules of source. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are fuzz seeds under fuzz/corpus, each an input the library parses, which tests/fuzz_corpus_test.py checks, and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, whose fetch command docs/source/conf.py gives. None is code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tree/main/fuzz/corpus
osps_qa_06_01_justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request that changes anything but prose, and its aggregate check, 'test: every job passed', is required on main. A pull request that changes only prose files nothing built reads skips the suite, and the aggregate check still passes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the tests and says which workflows run them and which gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md; standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040), read with gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/rulesets on 2026-11-07. GOVERNANCE.md reserves that bypass for an emergency, and it is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 28 of the 53 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v0.8.0.14 17 of 28, v0.8.0.13 11 of 25). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents each component, the cffi boundary and the release provenance. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* and *Trust boundaries* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. ARCHITECTURE.md's *The public surface* states what is public.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: claims, threat model, trust boundaries and how each common weakness is countered. SECURITY.md's *Limitations of the binding layer* records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names what is defended, the adversaries and what is not defended. Its *Trust boundaries* maps where untrusted input enters. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. A report triaged as easy to rediscover is fixed as soon as possible, and its advisory is published with the fix. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. GOVERNANCE.md's Roles says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository: GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, fixed in 0.8.0.10. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: A merged pull request that changes code under src/ also changes tests/, unless it leaves behaviour as it was: a docstring, a comment, a move, a removal or a refactor. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
release_notes_vulns_justification: The release notes name each advisory a release fixes: v0.8.0.10 names GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
repo_interim_justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests keep every report and its responses public and searchable. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub Issues, through the bug-report form. CONTRIBUTING.md's The issue tracker says where. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues
report_tracker_justification: Issues are tracked in this repository's GitHub Issues, with issue forms; cross-repository issues go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues
require_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org
roles_responsibilities_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
secure_2FA_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
security_review_justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30. The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues/1089
signed_releases_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and every GitHub release from v0.8.0 on a Sigstore provenance bundle. Release tags are signed from v0.8.0 on. SECURITY.md gives the verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest
sites_password_security_justification: The project runs no site that stores passwords; authentication is GitHub's, PyPI's and Read the Docs'. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
small_tasks_justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly, and ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No static-analysis finding is open: CodeQL has no open alert, and ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is measured (branch = true in [tool.coverage.run]) and the 100% gate includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: test.yml runs the suite on every push to main and every pull request that changes anything but prose. A pull request that changes only prose files nothing built reads skips the suite, and the aggregate check still passes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/test.yml
test_justification: test.yml runs the pytest suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, on every push to main and every pull request that changes anything but prose. It checks vectors published by the BIPs and other upstreams, and tests/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. A pull request that changes only prose files nothing built reads skips the suite, and the aggregate check still passes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100 fails the required check on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100 over the Python code, gated by test.yml on every pull request that changes anything but prose. The vendored C is tested by libsecp256k1's own suite, not by this gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (fail_under = 100 in [tool.coverage.report]) on every pull request that changes anything but prose. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested. The merged pull requests show recent changes landing with their tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: Over the last two releases, v0.8.0.13 and v0.8.0.14, 25 of 53 pull requests were approved by somebody other than the author, 47%, below the 50% the criterion asks (v0.8.0.14 11 of 28, v0.8.0.13 14 of 25); 16 were approved by somebody other than fametrano. Counted by merge time between release publications, over the same two-release window on every btclib-org project. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: PyPI packages are pinned in uv.lock and updated by weekly Dependabot pull requests that run the full suite. The vendored libsecp256k1 and secp256k1-zkp are git submodules pinned at a commit, and Dependabot opens a weekly pull request when upstream moves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
version_semver_justification: The first three numbers are the bundled libsecp256k1's own version, and a fourth counts releases of the bindings alone on it (0.8.0.1, 0.8.0.2, ...): neither SemVer nor CalVer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1#readme
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are signed from v0.8.0 on, and GitHub verifies each. RELEASING.md signs each tag with git tag -s and reads the signature back after the push. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tags
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been reported; the one advisory (GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c) is medium and was fixed on the day it was published.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. Issues 1228, 1229 and 1231, labelled security, are hardening against a caller's programming error, not vulnerabilities, and v0.8.0.13 fixes them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: The reporter of GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, pmazzocchi, is credited as finder on the advisory. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories/GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, reported privately by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, was fixed in v0.8.0.10 and published on 2026-10-03. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org) and the response times. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"], mypy with strict = true and pytest with filterwarnings = ["error"], each in a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"] and mypy with strict = true, both with zero findings allowed in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
